decisions.issues: Minor only: the topknot sits high on the crown but much of his curly hair falls loose around the neck, and there is faint warm shading on the jaw that reads as skin texture, not a beard. The moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, grey temples, silver chain, ivory conch-knife at the waist and the scar on the inner LEFT forearm all match. The room has lime-washed laterite walls, a dark timber ceiling, a closed shutter, a woven mat, a low table with string-bound palm-leaf bundles and a single open-wick lamp. There is no writing on the leaves. Hands are sound. A large clear plaster wall in the upper left has room for both long captions.

Both figures are tiny, as the script asks, so facial details cannot be checked at this scale. The small Nagoji wears white with a topknot. Revathi is in an indigo sari with a gold border and jasmine in her braid, and her tali is not visible. They walk toward each other from opposite ends of the tank path. The scene has two hawks circling, a morning sky, a tiled Kerala temple roof, a brass lamp-pillar, coconut palms and a stepped tank. There is no text. The upper half is open sky, with ample room for both captions.

Minor only: Revathi is shown already mounted rather than standing beside her horse (still reads as 'she has stopped' and sets up 2.3 riding away); her sandalwood hairline line and grey threads are not distinct at this size. Nagoji matches: topknot, grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, small flush gold stud, chain of office, ivory conch knife at waist. No tali on Revathi. Wide dusk sky across the upper middle and right gives ample room for four balloons.

Minor: faint stubble texture on Nagoji's jaw, still reads clean-shaven. Otherwise clean: jackfruit tree, laterite house and kalari weapon rack behind, Padmini with black coiled hair threaded grey, cream gold-bordered drape, stick, fingers on the green cloth as Nagoji takes it with sound hands; Nagoji with topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, flush gold stud, chain and conch-marked ivory knife. Light sky between the roof and the tree (upper middle) holds the two short balloons.

Minor issue: Revathi looks toward frame right, while 3.3 and 3.5 put Nagoji on the left looking right. The shot/reverse-shot does not quite line up, but this is a staging nicety, not a failure. Everything else matches: indigo and gold sari, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line, a few grey threads at the temple, no tali. The verandah, sunken kalari with boys and watching sisters, and women pounding grain are all there in late-afternoon light. No painted text. The hands are clasped and sound. Lettering space: open sky upper right (x 0.55 to 1.0, y 0 to 0.13) plus the plain roof tiles below it.

Minor issue: the grey at his temple is a little heavier than 'first grey', but it matches 3.5. Everything else matches: dry, arms-folded pose, Kerala topknot, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold stud, silver chain of office, ivory conch-marked knife at his waist (page 3, correct), cream mundu and shoulder cloth. Same verandah, courtyard and light as 3.2. No text in the art; the medallion carries a design, not letters. Lettering space: open sky upper right (x 0.5 to 0.9, y 0.02 to 0.18).

Three minor issues. (1) Nagoji's ear ornament is a tiny gold ball that sits a hair below the lobe rather than perfectly flush; at reading size (about 8 px) it reads as a small stud. (2) Revathi's grey threads do not show in this small side view. (3) Nagoji's topknot sits near the top edge (head at y 0.03 to 0.23), above the requested middle band. Around them: a bangled woman with a pestle, boys sparring in the kalari, girls watching, hanging brass lamps with open wicks, low warm light. Nagoji has topknot, curled moustache, clean chin, chain and knife; Revathi has no tali, coin necklace, jasmine braid and sandalwood line. Hands are sound. No painted text. The setting matches 3.2 and 3.3. No lettering in this panel.

Minor only. The brand and white scar show on the outer face of his crossed LEFT forearm rather than the inner side, but it is the correct arm. The brass standing lamps are lit in daylight. Nagoji matches the Ananthan Pillai sheet and the ch20 row: curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, a flush gold stud, a topknot with grey temples, the silver chain and the ivory conch knife at his waist. Minor only. Revathi's grey threading is a little more visible than 'a few threads'. Lettering space is moderate: a short balloon fits in the upper-left sky. The long balloon fits in the sky and dust plume between the rider and her hair, or in the pale dust at the lower left, as long as both stay clear of the rider and her face. She matches her sheet with no tali: indigo-and-gold sari, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, jhumkas and the sandalwood line. Clean pick. Nagoji matches the Ananthan Pillai sheet and the ch20 row: topknot high on the crown, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold stud, silver chain, white mundu and shoulder cloth, and the ivory conch knife at his waist. His left hand rests flat on the door frame and the anatomy is sound. He has the small smile the script asks for. The brand on the inner left forearm faces away, which is correct. The white-turbaned guard with a musket and the empty mats and carved seat match panels 5.1 to 5.3. The plain gold wall at upper right, above the lattice, is clear space for Nagoji's balloon. Minor: the topknot is a loose curly bun rather than a tight knot.

Acceptable, with small continuity flaws. The beat reads correctly: the shot is from behind Revathi, her hand rests on the back of the low carved seat at the head of the empty mats, and Nagoji stands small in the bright doorway. Revathi matches her sheet: indigo and gold sari, jasmine braid, gold armlet and bangles, gold earring, and no tali visible. At small scale Nagoji still shows his topknot, curled moustache, clean chin, ear stud, silver chain and mundu with shoulder cloth; his knife is not clearly readable. Flaws: (1) The door guard wears a red turban and a sleeved white tunic, where panels 5.2 and 5.4 show a bare-chested guard in a white turban. This is a background costume mismatch only. (2) Revathi is fully lit rather than the dark silhouette the script asks for. Her face is turned away, so her listed tail points to the right side of her head, toward the doorway. Balloon space: the upper-left lattice above and left of her head is mid-detail but covers nothing important, and the narrow plain wall between her head and the left door leaf can also take a balloon. Keep balloons off Nagoji in the doorway and off the guard.

Clean. Revathi matches the sheet and bible row: indigo sari with gold zari, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line at the hairline, no tali. Close, lamplit, troubled expression; courtyard at lamp-lighting with violet sky. Grey threads barely visible (minor). The long balloon fits in the clear violet sky at upper right, above the roofs.

Acceptable. Nagoji sits on the laterite steps looking down at the stone, hands clasped (anatomy sound). Acceptable. Like panel 4, Nagoji sits on the same steps in the same costume, now looking up and to the right toward the off-panel Revathi. v02 gets everything else right: Kayal has her muzzle in Nagoji's cupped palms, the face, moustache, clean chin, gold stud, topknot, grey temples, chain and conch knife all match, and the dusk stable setting fits. The problem is the brand on his inner LEFT forearm. It is drawn as a crisp emblem: a stem with a crossbar, a dot in a circle and a crescent, like a sigil or pseudo-glyph. The bible requires a pale puckered patch blurred past reading, with no letters and not a cross. The long white scar also runs on past the elbow onto the upper arm.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition exactly. Kayal stands at left with her muzzle pushed into Nagoji's cupped open palms. Nagoji stands at right in three-quarter view, looking down at her. He is bare-chested, with the cream shoulder cloth over his left shoulder, the topknot high on his crown, grey at the temples, the silver chain with its pendant, and the ivory-handled conch-pommel knife at his left hip. The stable roof and hanging brass lamp stay at upper left and the dusk sky at upper right. Fix only the brand. On the inner LEFT forearm, a hand's width above the wrist, draw it as a small, soft, irregular pale patch of puckered, rippled, raised scar tissue with blurred edges, like an old healed burn. It must form no shape at all: no symbol, emblem, glyph, letter, anchor, cross, crescent, ring or dot. Beside it, a single long thin white scar line runs along the inner forearm from the wrist to the elbow and stops at the elbow, never continuing onto the upper arm.

That breaks her sheet's long jasmine braid and panel 7.2, where the braid and grey streak are clear. His mundu and shoulder cloth are plain cream with no green or coloured stripes.

v02 is the only listed candidate and it is acceptable. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch20 @10.3- row: topknot with grey temples, thick curled moustache, clean chin, small flush gold ear stud, silver chain, white mundu and shoulder cloth, and no knife at his waist. Dhanaji matches too: white pagdi, short black beard, indigo quilted tunic, leather belt with talwar, and the gold hoop earring from his sheet. The beat reads clearly. Nagoji's two hands close Dhanaji's fist over the ivory knife handle, and the brand and scar sit on the near (LEFT) inner forearm. Dhanaji's head is bowed under the turban. Minor points: Dhanaji's look reads as downcast more than visibly swallowing. Lettering space is tight. The two Nagoji balloons will have to sit in the top band of roof tiles and sky, either top-left above the ladder workers or top-centre between the turban and Nagoji's topknot, and may spill onto the background garlands. They must not drop below about 0.22 of frame height near the faces.

Minor issues only. Padmini's hair is more grey on top than the 'black with grey threading' asked for, but her face, white sari with gold border, jasmine and planted stick all match. Nagoji sits cross-legged instead of kneeling, and no chain of office shows. The couple sit on either side of the fire with a gap between them, not side by side. Nagoji's moustache, clean chin, gold stud, topknot and plain white cloth are correct. The priest is clearly distinct and sits across the fire. De Lannoy, Ponnan and his two men, and Dhanaji stand at the back, left to right, readable by costume. Revathi wears no tali. The two captions fit in the sunset sky at the top right, above the wall and between the palms.
Her hands are mostly hidden behind the fire altar in the foreground. This is acceptable.
The bowed head and coiled hair fill the top centre, so the captions go in the sky at the top right or top left, or on the swept floor at the bottom left.

v02 (the only listed candidate) has three male hands: one comes in from the left frame edge and grips the left side of her neck, and two more come from separate forearms on the right, one pinching the thread and one below it. The cast is only Nagoji and Revathi, so one hand is extra. decisions.correction: HANDS, STRICT: draw exactly two hands in the whole frame, one left and one right, both Nagoji's, each joined by a visible forearm to the same body. He kneels at Revathi's right side and a little behind her, so both his bare brown forearms enter from that one side of the frame (with only an edge of his plain white shoulder cloth, no gold border, at the frame edge), and his two hands meet at the side of her neck, his fingers pulling the third knot of the yellow thread tight. No third hand, no forearm coming in from the opposite frame edge, no hand of the priest or anyone else, and Revathi's own hands are not raised to her neck. Keep everything else that worked: the tight close-up of her chin and throat with her face cropped at the mouth, the small gold tali pendant on its yellow thread worn high at the throat and clearly separate from the longer flat-coin necklace, the indigo silk sari with gold zari, the gold armlet, jasmine in her pinned-up hair, and the softly blurred firelit brass lamps and brick fire altar behind. Keep the upper right quarter as plain, softly blurred courtyard wall with no lamps or flames, for the long off-panel priest balloon.

This fixes the r1 failure. Revathi now sits on the verandah floor with her back to a dark wooden pillar and her knees drawn up, so the staging matches 14.1, 14.4 and 14.5. There is no railing. This fixes the r1 failure. Nagoji's ear now has a tiny flush gold stud on the lobe with nothing hanging from it. The composition is kept: Revathi half-risen at left, leaning toward him with her right hand held out and her left hand gathering the sari. Nagoji sits at right in a plain white mundu and shoulder cloth with no knife, looking up and taking her hand. He has his topknot, grey at the temples and a thick curled moustache. Minor issues: faint stubble shading on Nagoji's jaw, the same as in 14.1 and 14.4. Revathi's tali hangs on a thin gold chain rather than a yellow thread, as elsewhere on the page. There is no text in the art. Clear space: the large plain lamplit wall upper centre-right, above Nagoji, for his long balloon, and the night sky upper left for Revathi's short 'Come.'

The room matches 15.1 and 15.2: brass lamp on its stand, lattice window, carved bed and a jewellery stand holding the removed bangles and earrings. The braid is coiled and pinned up with jasmine, she sits with her back to him and is half turned, and the upper-left wall is clear for both balloons.

Clean. She pulls a pin from the coiled braid as her hair falls loose and dark down her side. The tali pendant is high at the throat and separate from the coin necklace. The armlets and sandalwood line match the sheet, and the earrings and bangles sit on the stand. The lamp and lattice window match the room. Both hands are sound. There is clear wall at upper left for the long balloon and above and right of her head for the short one.

Acceptable with minor notes. Nagoji's chin and jaw have faint stipple shading that reads as light stubble, not a beard. The thick curled moustache, topknot, grey temples, flush gold ear stud and plain white shoulder cloth are correct, and no knife is shown. Revathi's shoulders are bare with no blouse sleeve, unlike the short-sleeved blouse in 15.3 and 15.4. The sari still covers her and the look is period-plausible. The lamp behind them has three wicks, not one, but it is still an open-wick brass standing lamp. A sheer curtain at the far right edge hangs by a door frame, not over a bed canopy. He has crossed to her and holds her face steadily in both hands, and the arms resolve correctly. Clear wall right of Nagoji's head (upper right) takes the short balloon.

Minor: Nagoji's right shoulder and a little of his upper chest show above the cloth, the same as in panels 16.2 and 16.3, so it is consistent with the page. His chin has light jaw shading but no beard. The tali is one gold pendant necklace high at the throat, with no distinct yellow thread, which matches the neighbouring panels. The script beat is all there: dawn light through the lattice, children in the courtyard seen through the window, foot shadows in the light strip under the teak door, the lamp unlit, and his hand loose beside hers with no weapon. The topknot, grey temple, moustache and ear stud are correct. The upper-middle sunlit wall gives clear space for both captions.
